thread:
Chao: seeing sharp GPU pool drop in europe-north-1 — node count down 48% in the last 3m, autoscaler not recovering.
Maria: checking fleet metrics, I can repro error spikes on the control-plane -> 'heartbeat_timeout' from redis cluster.
Alex: is this the redis fail we patched last week? could be config drift after yesterday's deploy.
Chao: deploys look clean. redis master switched, replicas lagging heavily. KV cache writes failing intermittently.
statusbot: Status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/176953 — "EU-NORTH-1: degraded GPU capacity, some requests failing" :warning:
Sam: support is getting 15+ escalations. Customers reporting timeouts and higher latencies for large-batch jobs. Need ETA to communicate.
Maria: mitigation plan: 1) force failover to standby redis (manual), 2) cordon 6 affected nodes and migrate workloads to europe-west-2, 3) enable traffic-split 70/30 for critical customers.
Chao: can we do traffic-split without breaking sticky routing? some customers rely on pinned model version.
Alex: yes — use fallback routing with model-pin preservation: route primary -> europe-west-2 for new sessions, keep existing pinned sessions on local cluster with degraded performance.
Sam: pinging two enterprise accounts now; they want ETA and whether we'll waive overage charges.
support-bot: Triage note: escalation ticket #5462 opened, customers A+B+C added, severity P1 if latency >3s sustained.
Maria: I'm initiating manual redis failover now (command: `./ops redis failover --cluster eu-north-1 --force`). Expect ~30s window for slot reshard.
Chao: triggering node drain: `kubectl drain gpu-node-33 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — starting migration.
statusbot: Status page update posted: "Failover in progress, traffic being shifted to europe-west-2. ETA ~45min. We're prioritizing enterprise workloads and preserving pinned sessions where possible."
Alex: cost note — moving to europe-west-2 will use on-demand GPUs and we may hit a short-term +40% cost delta for the region. Finance aware?
Chao: finance pinged. We'll create a short billing waiver for impacted customers; ops cost will be absorbed for incident window.
Sam: customer update sent: "We're actively failing over traffic to another region to restore capacity. Estimated recovery in 45 minutes. Support team available 24/7."
Maria: Redis failover completed, replicas caught up. Starting health checks on cache-backed endpoints.
Chao: initial health checks pass for 60% of routes, continuing roll. Still seeing throttles on batch queue processors.
Alex: suggest enabling temporary batching-disable for non-critical jobs to free GPU slots: `featureflag batching:disable:noncritical`.
Sam: update to customers: "Partial recovery. Most realtime APIs restored. Non-critical large-batch jobs may be queued for up to 30-60 mins."
statusbot: Final status page update planned after verification.
Maria: final check — fleet at 92% capacity after migration, latencies near baseline for small requests. I'll re-open autoscaler logs to confirm root cause later.
Chao: creating follow-up ticket to review redis topology and autoscaler probes. Also add playbook step to run control-plane readiness check post-deploy.
Sam: closing escalation if no regressions in 1h. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
